calls.head: A shadow job for Mikheyev, Girgensons and Holmberg
calls.body: At home, the Lightning keep sending Mikheyev’s line (Mikheyev, Girgensons and Holmberg) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jon Cooper has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Canucks’ first line is DeBrusk, Pettersson (#40) and Lekkerimäki.

With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 34% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

calls.head: The Lightning should drive the play
calls.body: The Lightning have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Canucks the worst. Expect the Lightning to spend more of the night in the Canucks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

TBL.head: We gave Tampa Bay an 82% chance, and they delivered.

VAN.head: We gave Vancouver only an 18% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Kucherov’s two goals spark the Lightning
paras: Linus Karlsson struck first for the Canucks late in the first. Elias Pettersson (#40) made it 2-0 on the power play early in the second, but they didn’t score again. Nikita Kucherov scored later in the period and again just under five minutes later to tie it 2-2. Jake Guentzel put the Lightning ahead for good early in the third. Pontus Holmberg made it 4-2 with just over four minutes left, and that was that.

The Lightning drove the play, outshooting the Canucks 35-14, and the scoreboard caught up. Dennis Hildeby made 12 saves for the Bolts, and Kevin Lankinen stopped 31 of 35 at the other end. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Brayden Point, by our Swing measure. The Lightning improved to 6-2-0 and climbed to second in the Atlantic, while the Canucks dropped to 2-7-1, sixth in the Pacific.

items.text: The Canucks are winless in seven (0-6-1).
Jake Guentzel extended his point streak against Vancouver to six games.
NHL.com had projected the Lightning with 12 forwards and six defensemen, but they dressed 11 and seven.
Marco Rossi was in NHL.com’s projected lineup, but Arshdeep Bains played instead.
